EXTRACT FOR APPROVAL ROUTING, WITH AMENDMENT GP-01/A3 AND PURCHASE REQUEST PR-2026-4471

PART I — POLICY EXTRACT

1. Purpose and scope
1.1 This policy governs the purchase of all goods and services by Castellan Foods GmbH and its subsidiaries, excluding raw agricultural commodities bought on the commodity desk, intercompany charges, taxes and levies, payroll, and payments to public authorities.
1.2 The objectives are value for money, fair treatment of suppliers, segregation of duties and compliance with the Group's Code of Conduct and the Supplier Code.

2. Definitions
2.1 "Requester" — the employee who raises a purchase request in the e-procurement system (ProcureHub).
2.2 "Budget Holder" — the manager accountable for the cost centre that will bear the cost.
2.3 "Total Contract Value" or "TCV" — the total amount the Group may become obliged to pay the supplier under the contract over its maximum possible duration, including (a) all recurring fees for the initial term, (b) all recurring fees for any renewal or extension periods that the Group can trigger unilaterally or that occur automatically unless cancelled, (c) one-time fees such as set-up, implementation, onboarding, training or migration fees, and (d) any committed minimum volumes. TCV excludes VAT and other recoverable indirect taxes. Where fees are not fixed for renewal periods, the fee for the last year of the initial term is used.
2.4 Discounts. A discount reduces TCV only if it is unconditional and written into the order form or contract to be signed. Conditional, time-limited or verbal offers (for example "5% off if signed by the end of the month") are disregarded when calculating TCV, even if the Requester intends to meet the condition.
2.5 "Related Purchase" — a purchase from the same supplier (including its affiliates) for the same or a directly related business purpose.
2.6 "Sole-source" — a purchase where fewer than three compliant quotes were obtained without an approved sourcing waiver.

3. Competitive quotes
3.1 Purchases with TCV above EUR 25,000 require at least three written quotes or an approved sourcing waiver.
3.2 Framework agreements listed in Annex C have already been competitively tendered; call-offs under them need no further quotes.

4. Approval thresholds (by TCV)
Level 1 — up to and including EUR 10,000: Budget Holder.
Level 2 — above EUR 10,000 up to and including EUR 50,000: Department Head.
Level 3 — above EUR 50,000 up to and including EUR 150,000: Vice President of the requesting function jointly with the Group Finance Director.
Level 4 — above EUR 150,000 up to and including EUR 500,000: Chief Financial Officer.
Level 5 — above EUR 500,000: Executive Committee.
Each level includes the approvals of the levels below it in the workflow; the "required approval level" is the highest level the purchase reaches.

5. Anti-splitting
5.1 Requests must not be split to avoid a higher approval level.
5.2 Aggregation rule. When determining the approval level, the TCV of a request is added to the TCV of all Related Purchases approved in the 90 calendar days before the date the new request is submitted. The combined figure determines the required approval level for the new request. This applies whether or not the earlier purchase was deliberately split.

6. Additional reviews (independent of approval level)
6.1 Information Security review for any software, SaaS, hosting or data-processing service.
6.2 Legal review for contracts with non-standard liability clauses or a term longer than 36 months.
6.3 Sustainability screening for suppliers of packaging and logistics services.

7. Currency
Amounts in other currencies are converted at the Group treasury rate published on the day of submission.

8. Supplier onboarding
8.1 New suppliers must be created in the supplier master by the Supplier Master Data team before a purchase order can be issued. The Requester provides the supplier's legal name, registered address, VAT number, bank details on supplier letterhead, and a signed acknowledgement of the Supplier Code.
8.2 Bank details are verified by a call-back to a phone number obtained independently of the documents supplied. Changes to supplier bank details follow the same procedure.
8.3 Suppliers located outside the EU are screened against the sanctions lists before creation and monthly thereafter.

9. Purchase orders and invoices
9.1 No commitment may be made to a supplier before the purchase order is issued ("no PO, no pay"). Retroactive purchase orders are reported to the Audit Committee quarterly.
9.2 Invoices are matched three ways (purchase order, goods receipt or service confirmation, invoice). Price variances above 2% or EUR 500, whichever is lower, are blocked for Budget Holder review.
9.3 Standard payment terms are 60 days end of month; shorter terms require Group Treasury approval unless the supplier is a small enterprise as defined by the Group's SME policy.

10. Exceptions and breaches
10.1 Any purchase that did not follow this policy is recorded as a policy breach by Procurement Compliance, with the approval level that would have been required.
10.2 Repeated breaches by the same Requester are escalated to the Requester's VP and to Internal Audit.
10.3 Approval by a person at a lower level than required is not valid and does not bind the Group internally; the request must be re-routed.

PART 1 — NORTHERN UNION STRATEGIC GOODS REGULATION (SGR) — CONSOLIDATED EXTRACT FOR STAFF USE

Article 1 — Scope
1.1 The SGR controls the export and re-export of dual-use items listed in Annex I ("controlled items"), and of other items where Article 6 (restricted parties) or Article 8 (embargoes) applies.
1.2 An item is "subject to the SGR" if (a) it is located in the Northern Union (NU), (b) it was produced in the NU, wherever it is now located, or (c) it was produced outside the NU and incorporates NU-origin controlled content above the de minimis level in Article 4.
1.3 Items not subject to the SGR are outside its controls, except where another Article expressly provides otherwise.

Article 2 — Definitions
2.1 "Party to the transaction" — the purchaser, the intermediate consignee(s), the ultimate consignee and the end user.
2.2 "NU-origin controlled content" — components, software or technology of NU origin that are themselves listed in Annex I, valued at their purchase price when incorporated.
2.3 "De minimis percentage" — the value of NU-origin controlled content divided by the ex-works selling price of the foreign-produced item, expressed as a percentage.
2.4 "Restricted Parties List" (RPL) — the list published in Annex IV, including every name, alias ("also known as") and address shown in an entry. A party matches an entry if its name corresponds to the entry name or to any listed alias, or if it is located at a listed address and is under common control with the listed entity.
2.5 "Shipment value" — the invoice value of all items shipped at one time to one ultimate consignee.

Article 3 — Country groups (extract)
Group A: NU member states. Group B: close partner countries (Aldmere, Kestovia, Ruhland, Tessaly). Group C: other cooperating countries (Corvania, Marisco, Oronta, Pellan, Vasque). Group D: countries of concern for diversion (Draskel, Ilvaria). Group E: embargoed destinations (Karth, Soltane).

Article 4 — De minimis
4.1 A foreign-produced item is not subject to the SGR under 1.2(c) if its de minimis percentage does not exceed: 25% for destinations in Groups B and C; 10% for destinations in Group D.
4.2 There is no de minimis level for destinations in Group E, or for items incorporating NU-origin content classified 3E-901 or 5E-202 (all such items are subject to the SGR).

Article 5 — Licence requirements for controlled items (country chart, extract)
Category 3A-610 (thermal imaging components and modules): licence required for Groups C, D and E; not required for Groups A and B.
Category 5A-202 (encryption hardware): licence required for Groups D and E only.
Category 6A-003 (cameras, general): licence required for Group E only.

Article 6 — Restricted parties
6.1 A licence is required to export or re-export any item subject to the SGR where any party to the transaction matches an entry on the RPL. Licence applications under 6.1 are reviewed with a presumption of denial.

7.1 LVS (low value shipments): a licence required under Article 5 is not needed for shipments of Category 3A-610 or 6A-003 items to Group B or Group C destinations where the shipment value does not exceed EUR 5,000 and no more than two LVS shipments are made to the same ultimate consignee in a calendar year.

A.1 The bursary is paid at one of five levels:
    Level 0 — no award
    Level 1 — EUR 500
    Level 2 — EUR 1,200
    Level 3 — EUR 2,000
    Level 4 — EUR 3,000

PART B — DEPENDENCY STATUS
B.1 A student is INDEPENDENT if on the reference date (1 September of the award year) at least one of the following is true:
    (a) the student is 24 years old or older;
    (b) the student is married;
    (c) the student has at least one dependent child living with them;
    (d) the student was in local-authority care after their 16th birthday.
B.2 Otherwise the student is DEPENDENT.
B.3 For all purposes of these regulations, a registered civil partnership is treated exactly like a marriage, and a registered civil partner exactly like a spouse.
B.4 Dependency status is fixed on the reference date; later changes apply only from the next award year.

PART C — ASSESSED HOUSEHOLD
C.1 Dependent students: the assessed household is the parent(s) the student normally lives with, their spouse/partner if any, the student, and all other children living in that household.
C.2 Independent students: the assessed household is the student, their spouse (if any), and their dependent children (if any). Parents' income and household are NOT assessed for independent students, even if parental data was supplied on the form.
C.3 Household size = number of persons in the assessed household.

PART D — COUNTABLE INCOME
D.1 Countable income = sum over the assessed household (excluding children under 18) of: gross employment income for the previous calendar year (2025), net self-employment profit, pensions, and taxable benefits.
D.2 Excluded from countable income: child benefit; disability-related allowances; student loans and grants; earnings from the college's WORK-STUDY programme (for any student); one-off gifts under EUR 1,000.
D.3 Dependent students only: deduct EUR 2,000 from the household's countable income for each OTHER child of the household enrolled full-time in higher education.
D.4 Per-capita countable income = countable income ÷ household size, rounded to the nearest euro.

| Per-capita countable income | Level |
|-----------------------------|-------|
| up to 7,000                 | 4     |
| 7,001 – 10,500              | 3     |
| 10,501 – 14,000             | 2     |
| 14,001 – 18,000             | 1     |
| above 18,000                | 0     |

PART 1 — CUSTOMER DATA HANDLING STANDARD CDH-4 (v3.1)

§1 Scope
1.1 CDH-4 governs how Brightwater stores, uses, restricts and erases personal data of customers of the web shop and the retail stores.
1.2 Employee data, supplier contacts and job applicants are covered by separate standards (HR-7, PRC-2, TA-3).
1.3 Where CDH-4 requires a record to be "restricted", the record is moved to the restricted archive: it is kept, but may only be accessed by Finance, Legal or Privacy for the purpose for which it is retained, and it is excluded from marketing, analytics and customer service tools.

§2 Definitions
2.1 "Customer" — a natural person with a web-shop account or a loyalty card, identified by a Customer ID in the CRM.
2.2 "Account Data" — name, contact details, login credentials, saved addresses, saved payment tokens, preferences and loyalty data.
2.3 "Order Data" — baskets, quotes, order confirmations, delivery tracking and order-related customer service notes.
2.4 "Transaction Record" — the record of a completed sale for which an invoice was issued: the invoice itself, the corresponding payment record and the delivery confirmation. Baskets, quotes, pro-forma documents and orders cancelled before an invoice was issued are not Transaction Records, even if a payment was authorised and later released. A pro-forma document is not an invoice.
2.5 "Warranty Record" — product registration and warranty claim data needed to handle a warranty claim for a product sold to the Customer.
2.6 "Marketing Data" — newsletter subscription, consent log, campaign responses, segmentation attributes.
2.7 "Legal Hold" — an instruction from Legal to preserve all data relating to a specified Customer ID (or IDs) because of actual or anticipated litigation, a regulatory inquiry or a payment dispute.
2.8 "Verified Request" — a request that meets the verification requirements of §3.
2.9 "Invoice date" — the date printed on the invoice as its date of issue. It may differ from the order date and from the delivery date.

§3 Verification of requests
3.1 A request is verified if it is (a) submitted through the privacy form while the Customer is logged into the account, or (b) sent by e-mail from the e-mail address registered on the account and confirmed by the Customer through the six-digit code sent to that address.
3.2 A request sent from any other e-mail address or by post is verified only when the requester provides two of the following that match the CRM: an order number, the billing postcode, the loyalty card number, the last four digits of a saved card.
3.3 A request made by a third party on behalf of a Customer requires a signed authority from the Customer in addition to verification under 3.1 or 3.2.
3.4 Until a request is verified, no action is taken on it other than asking for verification. The response deadline in §7 runs from the date of verification.

§4 Erasure requests
4.1 On a Verified Request for erasure, Brightwater erases all personal data relating to the Customer ID, subject only to 4.2 to 4.4.
4.2 Legal Hold. While a Legal Hold covering the Customer ID is active, nothing is erased; all data relating to that Customer ID is restricted until the hold is released, and the request is then processed under 4.1.
4.3 Transaction Records whose retention period (§5) has not ended on the day the erasure is carried out are not erased but restricted; they are erased at the end of the retention period without a further request.
4.4 Warranty Records are retained (restricted) while the warranty period for the product plus six months is running.
4.5 Marketing Data is always erased immediately; the Customer's e-mail address is added to the suppression list in hashed form so that it is not re-imported from partner lists. The hashed suppression entry is not personal data held about the Customer for the purposes of 4.1.
4.6 An erasure request is not refused because the Customer has an open balance; Finance is informed and collects on the basis of the Transaction Records.
4.7 Loyalty points lapse on erasure. The Customer is told this in the acknowledgement.

§5 Retention periods
5.1 Transaction Records: ten (10) years from the end of the calendar year in which the invoice date falls.
5.2 Warranty Records: the warranty period of the product plus six months.
5.3 Customer service tickets not related to an order: three years from closure.
5.4 CCTV images from stores: 72 hours, unless a Legal Hold applies.

§6 Legal holds
6.1 Legal Holds are entered in the Legal Hold register by Legal, identifying the Customer ID(s) covered. A hold covers only the Customer IDs listed.
6.2 A Legal Hold remains active until Legal records its release in the register. Once released, the Customer's data is handled under the normal rules; release does not revive or cancel any pending request.

§7 Response deadline
7.1 Erasure is carried out and confirmed to the Customer within 30 days of the Verified Request.
7.2 Erased data may persist in encrypted backups for up to 35 days until the backup cycle overwrites it. This is not a ground for refusing or delaying erasure.

§8 Refusal
8.1 An erasure request may only be refused if it is manifestly unfounded or excessive (e.g. repeated identical requests within 3 months), as decided by the Data Protection Officer.

§9 Business accounts
9.1 For business accounts (account type "B2B" in the CRM), contact persons' data is erased on request, but Transaction Records of the business are retained for ten (10) years from the end of the calendar year of the invoice date regardless of Amendment 2026-1, because business customers' invoices are also retained under the commercial record-keeping rules of the purchaser's contract.

§10 Access and portability requests
10.1 On a Verified Request for access, Brightwater provides a copy of all personal data relating to the Customer ID within 30 days, including restricted records, in a commonly used electronic format.
10.2 Portability exports cover Account Data and Order Data provided by the Customer; derived segmentation attributes are excluded.
10.3 An access request made together with an erasure request is answered first; erasure follows once the export has been downloaded or 14 days after it was made available, whichever is earlier.

§11 Rectification and objection
11.1 Inaccurate Account Data is corrected within 10 days of a Verified Request.
11.2 An objection to marketing is handled as a request to erase Marketing Data only (4.5 applies); other data is not affected unless the Customer also requests erasure.
11.3 Where a Customer's wording is unclear ("stop contacting me", "remove me from your lists"), Privacy asks whether erasure of the whole account is intended before acting beyond 11.2.

§12 Store purchases without account
12.1 Receipts of store purchases paid by card are Transaction Records of the store; they are linked to a Customer ID only where a loyalty card was scanned.
12.2 Store purchases with a loyalty card scan appear in the ERP under the Customer ID with document type "POS".

(A) INCIDENT SEVERITY RUNBOOK ISR v5.0 (effective 1 February 2026)
======================================================================
1. Purpose
1.1 The severity of an incident determines paging, communication cadence, executive notification and the post-incident review format. The final severity is set at the post-incident review according to this runbook, based on the facts established after the incident; the severity declared during the incident is provisional.
1.2 This runbook covers availability, performance and data incidents. Security incidents (suspected or confirmed unauthorised access, data exfiltration, credential compromise) are classified under SICS-2 instead; where an incident is both, the higher of the two severities applies.

2. Definitions
2.1 "Active tenant" — a tenant that sent at least one API request in the 7 days before the incident started.
2.2 "Affected tenant" — an active tenant for which more than 5 % of its API requests failed (5xx or timeout) in at least one 10-minute monitoring window during the incident. Tenants with some failed requests below that rate in every window are not affected tenants.
2.3 "Enterprise tenant" — a tenant on an Enterprise plan with a signed Enterprise Master Services Agreement. Tenants on an Enterprise Trial (evaluation) plan are not Enterprise tenants for the purposes of this runbook.
2.4 "Payment processing" — the authorisation, capture, refund and payout APIs, and the ledger writes behind them. Invoicing, billing documents (invoice PDFs, statements), reporting and the merchant dashboard are not payment processing.
2.5 "Incident duration" — the time from the start of the first 10-minute monitoring window in which the incident's failure criterion was met to the end of the last such window. Alerting, acknowledgement and verification times are not part of the incident duration.
2.6 "Workaround" — a documented alternative that allows affected tenants to complete the affected operation without LatticePay intervention (e.g. a fallback endpoint), communicated to them on the status page or directly.
2.7 "Data loss" — loss of data that LatticePay had acknowledged as received. Data that can be restored automatically from the write-ahead log or replayed from the event archive, without manual reconstruction and with no more than 15 minutes of data affected, is "recoverable within RPO".

3. Base severity (impact)
3.1 SEV-1: more than 40 % of active tenants affected; or any unrecoverable data loss; or complete unavailability of payment processing in any region for 5 minutes or more.
3.2 SEV-2: more than 10 % and up to 40 % of active tenants affected; or 3 or more Enterprise tenants affected.
3.3 SEV-3: at least 1 % and up to 10 % of active tenants affected; or 1 or 2 Enterprise tenants affected.
3.4 SEV-4: fewer than 1 % of active tenants affected and no Enterprise tenant affected.
3.5 Where several criteria apply, the highest resulting severity is the base severity.

4. Adjustments (applied to the base severity in this order)
4.1 Duration: if the incident duration is more than 4 hours, raise the severity by one level (SEV-4 → SEV-3, SEV-3 → SEV-2, SEV-2 → SEV-1).
4.2 Workaround: if a Workaround was available to all affected tenants for the whole incident duration after the first 30 minutes, lower the severity by one level.
4.3 An adjustment never moves the severity above SEV-1 or below SEV-4.

5. Communication by severity
5.1 SEV-1: status page within 15 minutes; updates every 30 minutes; executive on-call paged; customer RCA within 5 business days.
5.2 SEV-2: status page within 30 minutes; updates hourly; customer RCA within 10 business days.
5.3 SEV-3: status page if more than 20 tenants affected; internal review only.
5.4 SEV-4: no status page; ticket-level follow-up.

6. Roles
6.1 Incident commander (IC): declares provisional severity, coordinates responders.
6.2 Communications lead: status page and Enterprise account managers.
6.3 Scribe: timeline in the incident channel.
6.4 Service owner: confirms the technical facts used for the final severity (affected tenants, duration, data impact) in writing before the review.
6.5 The IC's provisional severity is not changed during the incident for reclassification purposes; reclassification happens only at the review.

7. Post-incident review
7.1 A post-incident review is held within 5 business days for SEV-1 and SEV-2 incidents and within 15 business days for SEV-3. SEV-4 incidents are reviewed in the weekly operations meeting.
7.2 The review records the final severity, the facts on which it is based and the corrective actions.
7.3 Final severity drives the reliability scorecard: SEV-1 = 10 points, SEV-2 = 5, SEV-3 = 2, SEV-4 = 0.

8. Historical note
8.1 ISR v4.2 (in force until 31 January 2026) used "tenants with any failed request" as affected tenants and treated Enterprise Trial tenants as Enterprise tenants. It had no workaround adjustment and no floors.

Terms of Service v7.2, section 14 (Cancellation of annual plans)
14.1 An annual plan may be cancelled at any time by written notice. Cancellation takes effect 30 calendar days after the day on which the notice is received by Orbital Ledger; access continues until the end of the effective date.
14.2 Refund. For the days of the term that fall after the effective date, the customer receives a refund of the amount actually charged for the term, pro-rated by calendar days: (amount charged for the term) × (remaining days after the effective date) / (number of days in the term). 14.3 Early termination fee. If the effective date falls within the first six months of the term, a fee of EUR 75.00 is deducted from the refund. The first six months of a term beginning on the 1st of a month end on the last day of the sixth month.
14.4 No refund is made for terms that ended before the notice was received, nor for add-ons billed monthly.
14.5 Customers on monthly plans are not refunded; their cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing month.

2. Definitions. A "travel day" is a calendar day on which the employee is away from the home work location at midnight, except the departure day is also a travel day even when departure is after midnight local time due to a delayed carrier. A "provided meal" is food included without separately stated cost in lodging, conference registration, or carrier service; dietary unsuitability does not stop it being provided unless the accessibility office documented the restriction before travel. "Remote-site travel" means the destination is more than 80 road kilometers from both the employee's home and assigned office. "Timely" means received in the expense portal within 20 business days after the final travel day. Business days exclude weekends and the company closure dates listed in section 9.

3. Meal allowance. The standard allowance is 68 credits per full travel day. Departure and return days receive 75 percent. Deduct 20 percent for a provided breakfast, 30 percent for lunch, and 50 percent for dinner; percentages are of the unadjusted 68-credit daily allowance. The daily result cannot be below zero. Receipts neither increase nor decrease this allowance.

4. Lodging. Lodging is reimbursable up to 190 credits per night. Taxes stated separately are outside that cap. A conference hotel may be reimbursed up to 240 credits only when the booking was made before the conference block closed and the conference organizer named that hotel. Personal upgrades are never reimbursable.

5. Ground transport. Rail is preferred. A taxi over 55 credits requires either a transit-disruption record or remote-site travel. A manager's convenience statement is not a disruption record.

6. Pre-approval. A director may pre-approve lodging above the standard cap or taxi use without a disruption. The writing must identify the trip and a maximum amount. Pre-approval cannot waive timeliness, turn a personal upgrade into business expense, alter meal deductions, or override a later amendment.

7. Late claims. Finance must reject an untimely claim unless the portal was unavailable for at least four continuous hours on the submission deadline and the employee submitted by noon on the next business day. Manager absence, missing receipts, workload, or an email sent outside the portal does not extend the period.

DATA ACCESS STANDARD — 2026 consolidated edition
Article 1 — Scope. This standard applies to exports from Atlas, a system containing customer contact, billing, and service telemetry. The decision is made under the version in force when access begins, except a later emergency directive expressly made immediately applicable controls ongoing access.

Article 2 — Definitions. "Direct identifier" includes name, full address, email, telephone number, account number, or any stable value that another company can use to single out a person. A hash is still a direct identifier when it is stable across exports. "Aggregate" means every released cell combines at least 25 distinct customers after all filters. "Internal research" is work performed only by employees on company-managed devices, with no external recipient or publication. A contractor is external even if issued a company email address. "Short access" lasts no more than 30 consecutive days.

Article 3 — Baseline routes. Aggregate, non-identifying data may be approved by the analytics owner. Row-level telemetry without direct identifiers requires privacy review. Any direct identifier normally requires both privacy and security review, a recorded purpose, and deletion date. Marketing consent is irrelevant to security review.

Article 4 — Academic collaboration route. A university collaborator may receive row-level telemetry stripped of direct identifiers if a data-use agreement is executed before access, the ethics approval is current, and privacy approves the transformation. The analytics owner cannot substitute for privacy. No direct identifiers may use this route.
